reason: The gated uniform-preference SASRec achieved macro validation HR@10=0.5375, with Electronics weakest at 0.435; its prefix pooling ignores item order, motivating the proposed controlled recency experiment without establishing the cause of remaining errors. Historical preference-branch gains support preserving the projection and gate, while failed recency-weighted MultVAE experiments argue for changing only preference pooling, leaving supervision unchanged. Model design implements that change, and training/evaluation ensures correct diagnostics, checkpoint reconstruction, and generated inference.

plan.model_design: Replace only SASRec._prefix_mean(raw, keep) with a causal exponentially weighted mean of raw item embeddings within the existing truncated window, using fixed decay d=2**(-1/10) and preserving its name, arguments, and output shape. Initialize per-batch embedding sums S and scalar weights W to zero; at each position update S=d*S+raw_t and W=d*W+1 only for observed items, leave both unchanged for padding, and emit keep_t*S/W.clamp_min(1), retaining differentiability and using float32 accumulation for numerical stability under autocast. This introduces order-sensitive preferences without trainable pooling parameters; retain preference_proj, preference_norm, the feature-wise gate and its zero-weight/-2-bias initialization, the Transformer, item_bias, and candidate scoring unchanged. Preserve SASRec constructor compatibility and forward(self, seq), ranking_loss(self, seq, pos, negative), and predict(self, seq, candidates), adding only an optional trailing preference_half_life=10.0 constructor field if needed for explicit metadata. Keep embedding dimensions, attention blocks, dropout, uniform losses.mean() sampled-softmax supervision with 64 negatives, training-window sampling, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and gradient clipping unchanged, isolating pooling from the historically unsuccessful changes to recency-weighted supervision.
plan.training_evaluation: Update train_one metadata and PREDICTOR together with its writer in main so working/predict.py explicitly reconstructs the same fixed-half-life architecture, strictly loads checkpoints, and retains pack_history and dataset_name routing across all four categories; preserve existing function signatures and variable names. Revise verify_preference_branch to compare pooling against explicit normalized exponential weights, checking empty and singleton histories, repeated items, padding that neither contributes nor advances decay, a ten-observed-interaction age difference yielding a 0.5 weight ratio, causality, finite outputs, and branch gradients while preserving training RNG state. Retain verify_generated_predictor and check checkpoint-reloaded scores against generated predictor scores for all categories, updating diagnostic reference values from 0.5137/0.410 to the current 0.5375 macro and 0.435 Electronics results. Explicitly keep unchanged preprocessing seed 0, training and evaluation seed 42, supplied splits, all four separate category models and routing, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, SASREC_EPOCHS default 200, existing early stopping and HR@10/NDCG@10 checkpoint selection, runtime controls, and single-GPU execution within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Compare host-reported macro HR@10 and all category scores against the current model under the unchanged 200-user-per-category, 99-unique-negative, seed-42 evaluator, treating 0.545–0.550 as an unmeasured hypothesis and retaining identical history packing and learned scoring without hidden-test access, additional data, pretrained weights, or evaluator changes.
